title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 115 (Resolutions requiring special notice)

content.overview: Where the Act or the articles require special notice of any resolution, notice of the intention to move such resolution shall be given to the company by members holding not less than one per cent of total voting power or holding shares on which an aggregate sum not exceeding five lakh rupees, as may be prescribed, has been paid-up, and the company shall give its members notice of the resolution in the prescribed manner.
content.glance: Eligible members notify the company of intention to move a resolution requiring special notice; the company then notifies members in the prescribed manner.
content.study:
## Section 115 — Resolutions requiring special notice

Section 115 applies when a provision of the Act or the articles requires special notice. Members meeting the prescribed threshold (not less than one per cent of total voting power, or shares on which an aggregate sum not exceeding five lakh rupees as prescribed has been paid-up) give notice of intention to the company. The company then gives its members notice of the resolution in the manner prescribed (read with Rule 23 of the Companies (Management and Administration) Rules, 2014).

Special notice is procedural. For director removal, apply section 169 safeguards including the director's opportunity to be heard. Special notice alone does not pass the resolution.

This note is a focused study aid; the topic remains under source and current-law review.

examples.title: Threshold verification
examples.body: Members submit a special notice. The company verifies the prescribed member threshold, timing and service under current Rule 23 before processing. Educational illustration.

hypotheticals.question: A member circulates a proposal to shareholders but does not give the required notice to the company. Is section 115 complied with?
hypotheticals.analysis: No. Notice of intention must be given to the company by members meeting the prescribed threshold. Circulation to shareholders alone does not establish compliance.

misconceptions.trap: Treating special notice as itself passing the resolution.
misconceptions.correction: Special notice is a procedural precondition; the resolution must still be duly passed.
